title: Microsoft Purview: sensitivity label groups replace parent labels (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: Hold: the description overstates which differences in label scope cause migration to create a same-name sublabel. Microsoft specifies two particular scope conditions, which administrators need when deciding which labels to review before migration.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans a sensitivity labelling scheme consisting of labels and label groupings.
claims.quote: the sensitivity labeling scheme will be simplified to only consist of labels and label groupings.

claims.claim: The planned groupings let administrators organise and categorise labels.
claims.quote: These new label groupings allow admins to better organize and categorize their labels

claims.claim: Parent labels previously performed this grouping function.
claims.quote: These new label groupings allow admins to better organize and categorize their labels (previously done via parent labels).

claims.claim: A parent label configured for encryption is applicable for creation of a same-name sublabel during migration.
claims.quote: It's configured for label actions that include encryption, content marking, auto-labeling, and PowerShell advanced settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A parent label configured for content marking is applicable for creation of a same-name sublabel during migration.
claims.quote: It's configured for label actions that include encryption, content marking, auto-labeling, and PowerShell advanced settings.

claims.claim: A parent label configured for auto-labelling is applicable for creation of a same-name sublabel during migration.
claims.quote: It's configured for label actions that include encryption, content marking, auto-labeling, and PowerShell advanced settings.

claims.claim: A parent label configured for PowerShell advanced settings is applicable for creation of a same-name sublabel during migration.
claims.quote: It's configured for label actions that include encryption, content marking, auto-labeling, and PowerShell advanced settings.

claims.claim: A parent label included in a different publishing policy from its sublabels is applicable for same-name sublabel creation.
claims.quote: It's included in a different publishing policy from its sublabels.

claims.claim: Having a different label scope from its sublabels is sufficient for a parent label to create a same-name sublabel.
claims.quote: A sublabel is configured for a label scope that the parent label isn't configured for. Within the same label policy, the parent label has one or more scopes that aren't configured for any of its sublabels.
claims.fix: Replace 'or has a different label scope from its sublabels' with 'or has a sublabel configured for a scope the parent does not have, or, within the same label policy, has a scope not configured for any of its sublabels'. These are the specific scope conditions at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/migrate-sensitivity-label-scheme.

claims.quote: The resulting sublabel that's created has the same name, label GUID, and settings as the original parent label.

claims.claim: Existing GUID-based references to the applicable parent continue to identify the sublabel, not the new group.
claims.quote: Because label GUIDs are unique in your tenant, they are used by backend services and configurations to reliably identify a sensitivity label. To ensure business continuity post migration, the new sublabel inherits the GUID from the applicable parent label

claims.claim: Label groups do not themselves apply content protection settings.

claims.quote: This page will also alert you to any naming conflicts that need to be resolved before the migration.

claims.claim: Sublabels must have names distinct from their parent's name.
claims.quote: All sublabels must have a unique name from their parent label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft does not recommend editing label configuration during migration.

claims.claim: Sublabels in the same label group do not support the justification setting for lowering a label.
claims.quote: If you're using the modern label scheme that replaces parent labels with label groups, sublabels in the same label group also don't support the justification setting.
